teams.heading: Fiji seek defensive reset after conceding 326 points across 11 matches
teams.body: The Flying Fijians have shown significant scoring threat but fragile defence across their last 11 games. In that 11-match window, Fiji scored 315 points, averaging 28.6 points a game. However, they also conceded 326 points in those same fixtures, an average of 29.6 per match. The highlight of this recent run was a convincing home performance in September 2025 during the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage, where they beat Canada 63-10.

teams.heading: Beno Obano to exit Premiership as England career faces uncertainty
teams.body: Beno Obano has confirmed he will join French side Pau at the end of the upcoming season, casting doubt on his future within Steve Borthwick's setup. Due to the RFU’s strict policy prioritising domestic-based players, the 31-year-old prop faces a likely international exile. While Borthwick has occasionally accommodated players bound for France, he has increasingly focused on developing younger loose-head options, including Fin Baxter and Emmanuel Iyogun, to ensure long-term squad stability ahead of the 2027 World Cup.

teams.body: Former Ireland second-row Ryan Caldwell has opened up about his difficult transition to life after professional rugby, reflecting on a career marred by chronic injury and a subsequent struggle with addiction and depression. teams.heading: Gonzalo Quesada suspended following World Rugby match official abuse ruling
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has become the first coach banned under World Rugby’s new Match Official Abuse Sanctioning Process. The governing body handed the Argentine a two-Test suspension following his public criticism of referee Luc Ramos after the meeting with the All Blacks. As a result of this ruling, Quesada is prohibited from all match-day proceedings for the upcoming Test against South Africa. He retains the right to appeal the decision, though his status remains uncertain for the November campaign.

teams.heading: Tom Rogers eyes international return after switching to the Ospreys
teams.body: Following his move from the Scarlets to the Ospreys this summer, Tom Rogers is prioritising a return to the Wales squad. The back, who made history last November by scoring the first Test hat-trick against New Zealand by a player from the British Isles, has not featured for his country since that match. Admitting his recent uncapped appearance against the Barbarians was underwhelming, Rogers remains focused on his club form: "I just need to play well with the Ospreys."

teams.heading: Les Kiss makes nine changes as Tom Wright hits 50th cap
teams.body: Les Kiss has overhauled his side for the rematch against Argentina, making nine changes to the starting XV that won in Jujuy. Full-back Tom Wright reaches his 50th appearance for Australia, anchoring a back three alongside Max Jorgensen and Filipo Daugunu. Captain Harry Wilson returns at number eight, while Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Len Ikitau reunite in the midfield. “We’ve brought in some fresh bodies alongside some existing combinations as we continue to look to build Test experience across the group,” said Kiss.

teams.heading: Ardie Savea ruled out of fourth Test following shoulder injury
teams.body: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea will miss the final Test of the series in the United States after sustaining a shoulder injury in Saturday’s clash at FNB Stadium. Head coach Dave Rennie confirmed Savea will not travel with the squad to Baltimore, stating, “He certainly won’t be travelling to the States.” Rennie acknowledged the loss of his skipper but backed Wallace Sititi to provide cover, noting that the team is “not going to use that as an excuse” for the narrow 29-24 defeat.

teams.heading: Cheslin Kolbe ruled out as Springboks defeat All Blacks in Soweto
teams.body: The Springboks secured a 29-24 win over the All Blacks on Saturday, moving into a 2-1 series lead, but the triumph was marred by a significant injury to Cheslin Kolbe. Rassie Erasmus confirmed post-match that the fullback suffered a broken jaw. With the series finale scheduled for Baltimore, the coach has confirmed that Damian Willemse and Canan Moodie are ready to step in, while Herschel Jantjes will join the travelling squad to bolster the backline options.
